Director's Foreword —— Taoyuan Museum of Fine Arts —— Taoyuan Children's Art Center —— Hengshan Calligraphy Art Center —— General Aﬀairs —— Appendix
Unfolding the Multifaceted Presence of the Museum through Diverse Practices
In 2025, the Taoyuan Museum of Fine Arts (TMoFA) continued to deepen
every facet of its institutional operations. As the Taoyuan Children’s Art
Center (TCAC) and the Hengshan Calligraphy Art Center (HCAC) reached
greater operational maturity alongside ongoing preparations for the main
museum, we unfolded a spectrum of distinct yet mutually resonant
practices across our museum group through exhibitions, research,
collection building, education and outreach, international exchange, and
public services—forging ever closer connections between art, urban life,
and audiences across generations.
In terms of collections, TMoFA acquired 134 works by artists across
diverse regions, media, and generations, while continuing regular collection
inspections and conservation projects. In international exchange and talent
cultivation, the Taoyuan International Art Award entered its third edition and
received a record-high number of submissions; with the participation of
curators from international institutions, it continued to expand our
connections with creators worldwide.
Centered on children’s perception and exploration, the TCAC created
spaces that encourage children to actively observe, question, and
participate through diverse curatorial themes spanning nature, the senses,
play, and shifting perspectives. Among these exhibitions, When Art Meets
Nature and Mini BOOM! together won two Gold Awards and one Silver
Award at the US-based MUSE Creative Awards. The TCAC also embarked
on its ﬁrst transnational co-production with National Gallery Singapore,
expanding international collaboration and touring exhibitions.
The HCAC continued to broaden the diverse horizons of calligraphic art
between tradition and contemporaneity, introducing perspectives from
multiple generations through research-driven curation, open calls for
curatorial proposals, and its biennale mechanism. Born out of years of
dedicated research, Walking Their Own Paths: Women Calligraphers in
Contemporary Taiwan was selected by Artist magazine as one of the Top
Ten Publicly Organized Exhibitions of 2025, while The 2nd Hengshan
Calligraphy Biennale: Calligraphy in Movement: From Literati’s Desk to
People’s Streets further expanded the dialogue among calligraphy,
contemporary society, and everyday culture.
In education, outreach, and public participation, TMoFA connected artistic
resources more closely with schools, families, and communities through
initiatives such as “School Add-on,” museum–school collaborations, oﬀ-
campus cultural experiences, and exhibition-related educational programs.
At the same time, visitor research was integrated into museum
development to better understand the needs and expectations of diverse
audiences through their visiting behaviors, experiences, and feedback. In
2025, TMoFA inaugurated “Citizens’ Day” and “Neighborhood Day” to
deepen ties with surrounding neighborhoods and cultivate a vibrant
museum-centered community anchored by its venues.
Looking ahead, preparing for the main museum signiﬁes not merely the
completion of a new building, but the further integration of TMoFA’s
museum group. Practices across academic and collection research, multi-
venue perspectives, education and outreach, and international exchange
will together shape a more complete proﬁle for TMoFA.
We extend our sincere gratitude to all staﬀ members, artists, partners,
volunteers, and every visitor who has walked into the museum. May
TMoFA continue to connect the city through art, growing alongside citizens
as an open and vibrant museum for all.
LIN Yung-Neng
Director, Taoyuan Museum of Fine Arts

2025 年，桃園市立美術館（下稱桃美館）持續深化各項館務。隨著桃園市兒童美術館（下稱兒美館）與橫山書法藝術
館（下稱書藝館）營運日趨成熟，以及總館持續籌備，我們透過展覽、研究、典藏、教育推廣、國際交流及公共服務，
展開各具特色而彼此呼應的館群光譜，也讓藝術與城市生活及不同世代的觀眾建立更緊密的連結。
典藏方面，桃美館新增134 件來自不同地區、類型與世代藝術家的作品，並持續進行藏品點檢及修復等工作。在國際
交流與藝術人才培育方面「桃源國際藝術獎」邁入第三屆，獲得歷屆最高投件量，透過國際館舍策展人的參與，持續
拓展與全球創作者的連結。
兒美館以兒童的感知與探索為核心，透過自然、感官、遊戲與視角轉換等多元策展主題，創造兒童主動觀看、提問
及參與的空間。其中「在藝術中遇見大自然」與「迷你蹦！Mini BOOM!」獲美國「繆斯創意獎」（MUSE Creative
Awards）二金一銀；並首度與新加坡國家美術館展開跨國共製，拓展國際合作與巡展。
書藝館持續在傳統與當代之間拓展書藝的多元面貌，透過研究策展、策展徵件與雙年展等不同機制，引入多元世代的
不同觀點。其中，由多年研究成果孕生的「自由自在：臺灣當代女性書藝展」獲《藝術家》雜誌評選為2025 年度十大
公辦好展覽之一；「2025 橫山書藝雙年展：運動中的書法―從文人的案頭到諸眾的街頭」則進一步拓展書法、當代社
會與日常文化的對話。
教育推廣與公共參與方面，桃美館透過外掛學校、館校合作、校外文化體驗、展覽教育活動等，讓藝術資源與學校、
家庭及社區建立更多連結。同時將「觀眾研究」納入館務發展，從參觀行為、經驗與意見回饋，理解不同觀眾的需求
與期待。2025 年首度舉辦「市民日」與「里民日」，深化與鄰里社區的連結，並以美術館為基地，開展美術館生活圈。
面向未來，總館的籌備不只是新館舍的完成，更意味著桃美館館群的進一步整合。學術與典藏研究、多元館舍視野、
教育推廣與國際交流等不同面向的實踐，也將共同構成桃美館更加完整的面貌。
感謝所有工作人員、藝術家、合作夥伴、志工，以及每一位走進美術館的觀眾。期待桃美館持續以藝術連結城市，成
為一座與市民共同成長、開放而充滿活力的美術館。
桃園市立美術館館長
在多元實踐中，開展美術館的多重面貌

Annual Collection Inspection and Conservation
To verify collection metadata and track storage movements, TMoFA regularly documents the preservation condition of its
holdings. From August to November 2025, the museum conducted its annual collection inspection, performing sampling checks
across ﬁve categories: “Oil Painting,” “Watercolor,” “2D Mixed Media,” “Others,” and “Printmaking.” External experts and
scholars were appointed as annual inspection committee members to examine the physical objects and collection records item
by item alongside staﬀ from the Research and Collection Department. Across eight in-storage inspection sessions, condition
records were completed for 233 collection items, ensuring eﬀective management and enhancing the quality of collection care
and preservation.

TMoFA also commissioned professional art conservators to complete the
conservation of eight ink paintings from its collection in 2025. Because the condition
and treatment needs varied across works, reversible, safe, stable, and acid-free
materials were used throughout the process to ensure the stability and safety of
each painting. Treatments included cleaning unidentiﬁed stains, yellowing, surface
dirt, foxing, and mold; consolidating, ﬁlling, and inpainting areas of loss; and
replacing mounts with suitable, aesthetically harmonious mounting fabrics and acid-
free framing to preserve both the aesthetic value and cultural signiﬁcance of the
collection.
Conservation process: Consolidating the seal impressions.
Conservation process: Examining the backing paper structure.
Before conservation (left) and after conservation (right): The painting core suﬀered from yellowing,
tears, previous improper repairs, and extensive foxing across the colophon silk mount. Following
conservation, the work was restored to its hanging scroll format with properly adjusted proportions
among the painting core, colophon, and mounting silk, improving both long-term preservation
stability and overall visual harmony.

Located on the 3rd ﬂoor of the TCAC and open during regular museum hours, the Children’s Art Library departs from conventional library cataloging systems by

reading from the perspectives of shopping experiences, monster imaginations, and shifts in scale—and paired with interactive installations, reading sessions, and
workshops—these exhibitions encouraged parents and children to explore everyday life, emotions, and diverse ways of seeing the world through shared reading.

“School Add-on” is an experimental educational innovation project spearheaded by the Taoyuan Children’s Art Center. Continuing the spirit of transforming the museum
into an open classroom, it brings children, families, communities, and creators together into a shared learning site through workshops, co-creation projects, artist
participation, and talks. Centered on the theme “Together, Together with Children” in 2025, the project advanced from practicing “for children” to practicing “with
children”—inviting young visitors, community elders, artists, and museum staﬀ to co-build a pop-up playground. Through hands-on co-play, community co-practice, an
open playground, and a series of talks, the program explored intergenerational inclusion, children’s participatory design, art education, and multicultural collaboration,
demonstrating the museum’s potential as a platform for co-learning, co-making, and sharing.
Creating an inclusive environment through playful artmaking with diverse media.

Museum–School Collaboration
Since its opening, the Taoyuan Children’s Art Center has actively responded to the New Curriculum Guidelines’ vision of “cross-disciplinary and diverse learning”
by launching multiple museum–school collaboration programs integrated with local characteristics.
— Qingyuan Elementary School students simulating sound through
calligraphy —
— Museum–school curriculum at Qingpu Elementary School
introducing plant diversity —
In 2025, the Hengshan Calligraphy Art Center partnered with Qingyuan
Elementary School to launch the course Graphic Scores of Sound. Recording the
acoustic textures of a calligrapher’s creative process from grinding ink to brush
writing, the curriculum combined calligraphy with sound aesthetics to guide
students in creating “sound images” and “graphic score performances.” Developed
into a school-based local reading curriculum at Qingyuan Elementary School, the
project enabled children to experience the contemporary vocabulary of calligraphic
art starting from listening.
Meanwhile, the Taoyuan Children’s Art Center drew upon the farming heritage of
the Qingpu area in collaboration with the art collective Rivers and Lakes Open
Studio. By observing plant patterns and learning about natural materials and
growth cycles, students cultivated their own pots of rice on campus and engaged
in spatial exploration activities—sensing space and landscape with their bodies to
gain a deeper understanding of Qingpu’s cultural and historical landscape.
Culminating in the design of the “Little Qingpu Plant Keeper” activity sheet, the
program guided students to learn about their local environment and envision
possibilities for future living.

art and embark on a rich visual journey.

Reimagining the Children’s Encyclopedia
Taking the 40th anniversary of the Echo Encyclopedia as
its starting point, the exhibition invited eight artists and
collectives to engage in dialogue with this classic
publication. Through contemporary artistic practices, each
artist addressed and questioned “Place,” “World,” and
“Future,” rearticulating knowledge through diverse artistic
forms to oﬀer open perspectives for viewing.
When Art Meets Nature
When Art Meets Nature is an international children’s art
special exhibition marking the ﬁrst collaboration between
TMoFA and National Gallery Singapore. Featuring works
by ﬁve artists from Taiwan and Singapore centered on
“nature, environment, ecology, and sustainability,” it
inspires sensitivity and reﬂection on artistic creation and
contemporary environmental issues.
INKFINITY: International Calligraphy
Masters Exhibition
Bringing together master calligraphers from nine regions—
China,
Japan,
Korea,
Taiwan,
Malaysia,
Singapore,
Indonesia, Vietnam, and Argentina—the exhibition presents
the diverse expressions and developmental trajectories of
contemporary calligraphic art.
Breath and Brushstrokes: Chu Chen-Nan
Calligraphy Art Exhibition
Featuring a curated selection of nearly 60 calligraphic
works by Taiwanese painting and calligraphy artist CHU
Chen-Nan, this catalogue is organized around the theme of
“the present moment” across ﬁve exhibition sections,
highlighting
the
pioneering
spirit,
creativity,
and
contemporaneity of the artist’s aesthetic sensibility.
Shuhari: Ro Boku’s Writing in Art World
Combining mixed media with large-scale calligraphic
installations, Japanese artist Ro Boku breaks through
traditional writing media to open up new expressive
languages and possibilities for calligraphy, demonstrating
its diverse presence and future potential in contemporary
society.
Spilled Words All Over the Floor: Chang
Tien-Chien
Through a personal calligraphic vocabulary, CHANG Tien-
Chien re-examines how written characters are viewed and
understood, expanding the expressive possibilities of
calligraphy in a contemporary context. From text selection,
brush writing, and mounting to exhibition design, the
catalogue presents the multifaceted ways calligraphy serves
as both script and poetic imagination.
